# SOP-P2-L2-04 Shift handover - Ring Rolling line
Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P2, line P2-L2  
Equipment: EQ-P2-L2-IH01, EQ-P2-L2-HT02, EQ-P2-L2-RR03

1. Purpose and scope  
   1.1 Purpose: Ensure safe, complete, and auditable shift handovers for the Ring Rolling line (P2-L2) covering induction heater, heat treat furnace, and radial ring rolling mill.  
   1.2 Scope: Applies to operators, lead hands, and maintenance personnel assigned to EQ-P2-L2-IH01, EQ-P2-L2-HT02, EQ-P2-L2-RR03 during shift change at Plant P2, line P2-L2. Refer to ECN-2026-031 for recent configuration changes and QS-PROC-07 for quality handover expectations. Use SOP-P2-L2-01 for routine start/stop procedures.

2. Background and rationale  
   2.1 Rationale: Incomplete handovers increase risk of process upset, quality escapes, and unsafe conditions. This SOP standardizes the exchange of process state, anomalies, and action items to reduce risk and support traceability.  
   2.2 Relationship to other documents: Changes controlled through ECN-2026-031. Quality acceptance criteria are specified in QS-PROC-07. Start/stop and permit steps are in SOP-P2-L2-01.

3. Preconditions (must be verified before handover begins)  
   3.1 Outgoing operator has completed end-of-shift checklist and initialed the logbook.  
   3.2 All critical alarms acknowledged and logged in the shift record.  
   3.3 Temporary barriers and lockout tags removed only if clearance was granted and documented.  
   3.4 Lubricant confirmation for equipment: The lubricant part number for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L2-HT02) is CFW-LUB-376. The lubricant part number for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #3 (EQ-P2-L2-RR03) is CFW-LUB-101. Verify stock and replenish if below normal supply on the visual inventory board.

4. Personal protective equipment (PPE) required during handover  
   4.1 Minimum PPE: safety glasses, steel toe boots, high-visibility vest, hearing protection as required by local signage.  
   4.2 Additional PPE where applicable: heat-resistant gloves when accessing hot-process zones, face shield when cleaning stray scale, cut-resistant gloves for maintenance bridging. Use the PPE matrix in QS-PROC-07 for role-based specifics.

5. Handover steps (numbered)  
   5.1 Initiation (outgoing operator)  
       5.1.1 Stop nonessential operations and stabilize line in controlled state per SOP-P2-L2-01.  
       5.1.2 Complete the end-of-shift checklist on the green handover form and initial every completed item. Note any in-progress corrective actions.  
       5.1.3 Inspect EQ-P2-L2-IH01, EQ-P2-L2-HT02, EQ-P2-L2-RR03 for visible leaks, abnormal noise, and unsecured guards. Document findings.  
   5.2 Communicate process state (face-to-face recommended)  
       5.2.1 Provide current product batch identifier and count, including parts processed in the last hour and any deviations from target dimensions or finish. Cite nonconformance items in the log.  
       5.2.2 Describe any recent interventions: maintenance calls, tool changes, and tamper events. Reference work orders or ECN-2026-031 for configuration changes.  
       5.2.3 Review alarm history and actions taken; confirm outstanding alarms are assigned and logged.  
   5.3 Special items for equipment (examples and rationale)  
       5.3.1 EQ-P2-L2-HT02: Confirm thermal ramp was completed and record condition of thermocouple junctions. Note the lubricant part number for Ring Rolling heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L2-HT02) is CFW-LUB-376. If lubricant was serviced during the shift, log lot number and dispenser used.  
       5.3.2 EQ-P2-L2-RR03: Verify radial guides and clamping are in the safe position and document any misalignment events. The lubricant part number for Ring Rolling radial ring rolling mill #3 (EQ-P2-L2-RR03) is CFW-LUB-101. Record lubricant batch and container ID if changed.  
       5.3.3 EQ-P2-L2-IH01: Confirm induction coil area is clear and shielding intact; document any observed coil wear or eccentricity issues.  
   5.4 Transfer of responsibility  
       5.4.1 Incoming operator reads and acknowledges the outgoing operator’s entries aloud and signs the handover form.  
       5.4.2 Outgoing operator confirms transfer by signing and stamping the form. Both retain copies as record.  
       5.4.3 If unresolved safety or quality risks remain, postpone transfer until mitigations are in place or escalate per QS-PROC-07.

6. Examples and common scenarios  
   6.1 Example: If a lubricant change was made on EQ-P2-L2-RR03, the outgoing operator notes CFW-LUB-101, lot number, and dispenser ID on the form. The incoming operator verifies lubricant container labeling before accepting the line.  
   6.2 Example: If a small dimensional drift was observed, record measurement trend and immediate containment actions; notify quality per QS-PROC-07 and reference any related ECN-2026-031 revisions if interim settings were adjusted.

7. Records to keep and retention  
   7.1 Green handover form: retained on-site in the shift binder for line P2-L2 and digitized into the MES within the same shift.  
   7.2 Maintenance tags and work orders: attach copies to the handover packet.  
   7.3 Lubrication change logs: include part numbers CFW-LUB-376 and CFW-LUB-101 entries where applicable.  
   7.4 Where deviations affect product quality, file a nonconformance report per QS-PROC-07 and link to ECN-2026-031 if a configuration change is initiated.

8. Sign-off (required)  
   8.1 Outgoing operator name, signature, time, and badge ID.  
   8.2 Incoming operator name, signature, time, and badge ID.  
   8.3 Lead or supervisor acceptance signature and time. Supervisor confirms that preconditions in section 3 were met before final acceptance.

9. Training and compliance  
   9.1 Operators must be trained on this SOP and demonstrate a supervised handover per SOP-P2-L2-01 before unsupervised transfers. Training records maintained per QS-PROC-07.

10. Audit and review  
   10.1 Handover records subject to periodic audit. Noncompliance findings shall be handled following QS-PROC-07 and any required engineering changes initiated via ECN-2026-031.
